text:
katie: Heads up — seen a 3x spike in tiny-pod evictions in ap-southeast1 over the last hour. Mostly tiny GPU jobs (gpu:1, cpu:1) getting preempted immediately after scheduling. Ops-bot: alert: evictions > 200 in 1h for cluster=ap-southeast1
leo: ack. timeline?
katie: started ~10:12 UTC. preemptions coincide with a label rollout (node.k8s.redwood/zone-batch=true) we pushed at 10:00.
raj: hmm could be scheduler packing change or label causing affinity to scatter — any eviction reason logs?
katie: logs show "Preemption" and a lot of "failed to fit" from scheduler. snippet:
```
E1001 10:15:33  scheduler.go:423] Pod default/trial-job-92 failed to fit: NodeAffinity conflict
```
maria: can you run a prometheus query? something like:
```
sum(rate(kube_pod_evictions_total{reason="Preempted"}[5m])) by (node)
```
ben: I ran a quick query — top nodes are those with the new label, and they have many tiny pods spread across many racks. pattern looks like fragmentation: too many small pods scattered, leaving expensive 8GPU instances partially used.
leo: so it's a packing/placement skew after label rollout. scheduler probably balances across label=true nodes, causing small pods to be spread instead of binpacked.
katie: probable. immediate mitigation: revert the label rollout? risky for the rollout users. alternative: tweak scheduler topology weight or add a temporary PreemptionPolicy tweak.
raj: quick workaround: set `PreferNoSchedule` taint on label=true nodes to reduce new placements, then drain and consolidate into other nodes. but that might increase latency for batch starts.
maria: another idea — lower `topologySpread` weighting for tiny pods so scheduler prefers binpacking by node instead of spreading. any way to target only GPU tiny pods?
ben: we can add a pod admission controller mutation for the small GPU pod class (annotation) to set packing hints: `scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/affinity: pack-small-pods=true` and config our scheduler to respect that.
leo: operationally fastest: increase `preemptionGracePeriodSeconds` and relax scheduling backoff so they don't get evicted immediately?
katie: preemptionGrace would reduce flapping but still wastes GPU time and cost.
katie: cost angle — if we move these tiny pods to Dedicated reserved pools (monthly commit), we avoid preemptions but cost goes up ~30% vs current spot-ish nodes.
raj: can we create a micro-pool of mixed small-instance nodes (4xGPU) and mark it as preferred for tiny GPU pods? autoscaler can spin up a few to absorb spike.
maria: yes autoscaler policy change is doable, but autoscaler will take 6-8 min to warm. need something shorter term.
ben: plan proposal:
1) mark label=true nodes with `PreferNoSchedule` taint to stop new placements (5m)
2) run a controller to re-annotate existing tiny pods with packing hint (10m) and kick a gentle reschedule when nodes have capacity
3) spin one small dedicated pool via autoscaler (15m)
4) monitor evictions and cost delta for 2h, roll back if worse
leo: I'll own step 1+2.
katie: I'll monitor evictions and heapster metrics, will alert on >20% drop in usable GPUs
ops-bot: deploybot: canary scheduler-config change queued by leo — run in ap-southeast1-canary group
katie: thanks. leo, ping when you've applied taint so SRE can watch. also capture a timestream of pod distribution: `kubectl get pods -A -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running | grep gpu` and snapshot.
leo: doing now. will post updates. :thumbsup:
katie: update 10:36 UTC — taint applied to 6 nodes, incoming tiny pods rate dropped ~60%, evictions down 40% in 10m.
raj: nice. next steps still to re-annotate and run canary scheduler tweak.
before we do heavy config, let's write an incident doc (short) and link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/packing-frag
maria: noted. I'll draft postmortem template after 2h window.
katie: thanks team — keep threads light here and use #incidents if it escalates.
